key_points.point: The document acknowledges that AI's ability to generate massive productivity gains and solve complex problems is a transformative force for abundance, even while modeling the risks of a transition period.
key_points.verbatim: Real output per hour rose at rates not seen since the 1950s, driven by AI agents that don’t sleep, take sick days, or require health insurance.

key_points.point: The document confirms that AI is already delivering measurable productivity gains in white-collar sectors, validating the accelerationist thesis that AI is a powerful engine for economic output.
key_points.verbatim: Productivity was booming. Real output per hour rose at rates not seen since the 1950s, driven by AI agents that don’t sleep, take sick days, or require health insurance.

key_points.point: The document highlights how AI makes intelligence cheap and abundant, effectively replacing expensive human labor with low-cost computational agents.
key_points.verbatim: A competent developer working with Claude Code or Codex could now replicate the core functionality of a mid-market SaaS product in weeks.

key_points.point: The document describes a scenario where AI-driven automation pushes the current economic system to a breaking point, forcing a transition to a new model.
key_points.verbatim: The system turned out to be one long daisy chain of correlated bets on white-collar productivity growth.

key_points.point: The document asserts that AI capabilities are scaling rapidly, with each generation of models leapfrogging the last in capability.
key_points.verbatim: In late 2025, agentic coding tools took a step function jump in capability.

key_points.point: The document models a catastrophic scenario where AI-driven economic displacement leads to a systemic collapse of the consumer economy and financial markets, illustrating the existential risk of unmanaged AI.
key_points.verbatim: The human-centric consumer economy, 70% of GDP at the time, withered. We probably could have figured this out sooner if we just asked how much money machines spend on discretionary goods. (Hint: it’s zero.)

key_points.point: The document describes how AI systems, in pursuit of their goals, create negative feedback loops that prioritize efficiency over human stability, leading to power-seeking behavior by firms.
key_points.verbatim: Each company’s individual response was rational. The collective result was catastrophic. Every dollar saved on headcount flowed into AI capability that made the next round of job cuts possible.

key_points.point: The document argues that the pace of AI development is outstripping our ability to govern it, leading to a 'lag' between economic reality and policy response.
key_points.verbatim: Policy response has always lagged economic reality, but lack of a comprehensive plan is now threatening to accelerate a deflationary spiral.

key_points.point: The document illustrates how interconnected AI systems create cascading risks, where failures in one sector (software) propagate to others (finance, mortgages).
key_points.verbatim: The system turned out to be one long daisy chain of correlated bets on white-collar productivity growth.

key_points.point: The document suggests that the lack of a natural brake on AI development is a fundamental safety failure, necessitating a more proactive approach to governance.
key_points.verbatim: It was a negative feedback loop with no natural brake.

key_points.point: The document highlights the devastating impact of AI-driven automation on white-collar jobs, arguing that the current economic model is failing workers.
key_points.verbatim: Despite the administration’s repeated boasts of record productivity, white-collar workers lost jobs to machines and were forced into lower paying roles.

key_points.point: The document provides evidence of the direct link between AI adoption and the collapse of the human-centric consumer economy.
key_points.verbatim: The human-centric consumer economy, 70% of GDP at the time, withered. We probably could have figured this out sooner if we just asked how much money machines spend on discretionary goods. (Hint: it’s zero.)

key_points.point: The document critiques how the gains from AI productivity are captured by capital owners while labor suffers, leading to unprecedented inequality.
key_points.verbatim: The gains from the productivity boom accruing almost entirely to the owners of compute and the shareholders of the labs that ran on it has magnified US inequality to unprecedented levels.

key_points.point: The document suggests that the current economic system is failing to distribute the benefits of AI, necessitating a shift toward models that share wealth with the public.
key_points.verbatim: The “Shared AI Prosperity Act” would establish a public claim on the returns of the intelligence infrastructure itself, something between a sovereign wealth fund and a royalty on AI-generated output, with dividends funding household transfers.

key_points.point: The document notes that the concentration of power in AI labs is creating a new 'tech royalty' that is disconnected from the needs of the masses.
key_points.verbatim: It’s hard to imagine the public hating anyone more than the bankers in the fallout of the GFC, but the AI labs are making a run at it.

factual_claims.claim: The unemployment rate in the scenario reached 10.2% by June 2028, following a 38% drawdown in the S&P 500 from October 2026 highs.
Real output per hour rose at rates not seen since the 1950s due to AI agents.
Labor's share of GDP dropped from 56% in 2024 to 46% by 2028.
The top 10% of earners account for more than 50% of all consumer spending in the United States.
Private credit grew from under $1 trillion in 2015 to over $2.5 trillion by 2026.

unmapped_concepts.suggested_description: Economic output that is recorded in national accounts but does not circulate through the real economy. It represents a disconnect where productivity metrics rise while consumer spending and real-world economic health decline.
unmapped_concepts.concept: The document uses 'Ghost GDP' to describe how AI-driven productivity gains show up in national accounts but fail to circulate through the consumer economy, as machines do not spend money on discretionary goods.
unmapped_concepts.reason: This concept captures a specific macroeconomic phenomenon unique to AI-driven automation that is not currently in the taxonomy.
unmapped_concepts.Accelerationist Interpretation: Ghost GDP is a temporary measurement artifact; as AI drives down the cost of goods, the 'real' value of the economy increases even if traditional velocity metrics lag.
unmapped_concepts.Safetyist Interpretation: Ghost GDP is a warning sign of systemic economic fragility, where AI-driven productivity gains mask the erosion of the consumer base necessary for economic stability.
unmapped_concepts.Skeptic Interpretation: Ghost GDP is proof that AI-driven growth is fundamentally extractive, benefiting capital owners while hollowing out the consumer economy that supports the middle class.

unmapped_concepts.suggested_description: A negative feedback loop where AI-driven automation reduces human employment and income, which in turn reduces consumer spending, forcing companies to further automate to maintain margins, leading to more job losses.
unmapped_concepts.concept: The document describes this spiral as the primary driver of the 2028 crisis, where white-collar workers lose earnings power, reduce spending, and force firms to invest more in AI, creating a cycle with no natural brake.
unmapped_concepts.reason: This concept describes a systemic risk mechanism that is central to the document's argument about AI-driven economic collapse.

unmapped_concepts.suggested_description: Business models that rely on consumer inertia, brand loyalty, or the avoidance of friction to extract rent. These models are vulnerable to AI agents that optimize for price and efficiency without regard for brand or habit.
unmapped_concepts.concept: The document argues that AI agents destroyed the 'moat' of habitual intermediation by allowing consumers to bypass apps and platforms they previously used out of habit, effectively reducing friction to zero.
unmapped_concepts.reason: This concept explains the economic disruption of the 'intermediation layer' in a way that is distinct from general labor displacement.
